objects.description: No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only declares two free functions (encrypt and decrypt) inside namespace esphome::xxtea. Built-in types (uint32_t, size_t) are referenced from standard headers and are not defined here.

functions.name: esphome::xxtea::encrypt
functions.signature: void esphome::xxtea::encrypt(uint32_t *v, size_t n, const uint32_t *k)
functions.description: Encrypts a block of data in place using the XXTEA algorithm and a 256-bit key. The data is provided as an array of 32-bit words and will be overwritten with the ciphertext. Typical usage is to pack plaintext bytes into 32-bit words, call this function with the word count and an 8-word key, and then use the resulting encrypted words as needed. Notes: byte/word packing, padding, and endianness expectations are not documented here and may need to match the implementation; the function does not return status.
requirements: v must point to a writable buffer containing at least n 32-bit words; the buffer will be modified in place.
If n > 0, v must be non-null.
k must be non-null and must point to at least 8 32-bit words (256-bit key).
Callers must ensure it is acceptable to overwrite the input buffer with encrypted output.
No error/status is returned; callers cannot detect failures via return value.

functions.name: esphome::xxtea::decrypt
functions.signature: void esphome::xxtea::decrypt(uint32_t *v, size_t n, const uint32_t *k)
functions.description: Decrypts a block of data in place using the XXTEA algorithm and a 256-bit key. The input is an array of 32-bit words of ciphertext; the buffer is overwritten with the decrypted plaintext. Typical usage is to supply the same 8-word key that was used for encryption and the same word count as used during encryption. Notes: byte/word packing, padding, and endianness expectations are not documented here and must match those used at encryption; the function does not return status.
requirements: v must point to a writable buffer containing at least n 32-bit words; the buffer will be modified in place.
If n > 0, v must be non-null.
k must be non-null and must point to at least 8 32-bit words (256-bit key).
Ciphertext must have been produced by the same algorithm and key to obtain meaningful plaintext.
No error/status is returned; callers cannot detect failures via return value.
